tagline: Champagne capital of the world, crowned by a Gothic masterpiece

taxi.fareNote: Official metered taxis wait at ranks near the station and cathedral; can also be booked by phone or app.

emergency.note: The EU-wide emergency number 112 also works nationwide and connects to English-speaking operators.

hood_desc: The historic core around the great Gothic cathedral where 25 French kings were crowned, packed with medieval lanes, museums, and champagne cellars open for tours.
Reims' liveliest strip, a long pedestrian square lined with brasseries, bars, and cafés that fills up every evening, especially on weekends.
A quieter southern quarter anchored by the Romanesque-Gothic Basilique Saint-Rémi, a UNESCO-listed abbey church and the city's oldest building.
Home to the restored Art Deco covered market hall, plus surrounding streets with local shops, bakeries, and produce stalls.
A leafy, upscale residential area bordering the Parc de Champagne park, with grand champagne-house mansions and a slower pace.
lodging: Best Western Hôtel de la Paix

transit.hours: Citura network runs roughly 5am-midnight; trams every 6-8 minutes at peak
transit.pay: Single tickets, day passes, or contactless bank-card tap on trams and buses; tickets also sold via the Citura app
transit.note: Two tram lines (A and B) link the station to outlying districts; buses cover the rest of the city

train: High-speed TGV from Paris Gare de l'Est, ~45 min direct to Reims Centre; TGV Champagne-Ardenne station on the outskirts also links to CDG airport and southern France
bus: FlixBus and regional coaches connect to Paris, Charleville-Mézières, and other regional cities

tip.r: A service charge is included by law in restaurant bills; rounding up or leaving a few euros for good service is appreciated but not required.

tagline: Ivory Coast's serene political capital, home to the world's largest basilica

taxi.fareNote: Shared woro-woro taxis run fixed routes for small flat fares; individual chartered taxis should have the fare agreed before departure, as meters are rare.

emergency.note: Emergency response can be slow outside the main hospital; the Yamoussoukro University Hospital Center (CHR) is the primary referral facility.

hood_landmark.Millionnaire: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace

hood_desc: The city's showpiece district, built around the immense Basilica of Our Lady of Peace, a near-replica of St. Peter's in Rome commissioned by President Houphouët-Boigny.
The administrative heart of the city, home to government ministries, the Presidential Palace, and its famous lake of sacred crocodiles.
A planned residential district near the Félix Houphouët-Boigny Foundation golf course, quieter and greener than the city center.
An older, predominantly Muslim trading quarter with a lively market and the Grand Mosque, reflecting the city's northern Ivorian trade links.
A busy commercial and residential neighborhood centered on Yamoussoukro's main market, with small bars, eateries, and everyday shops.

transit.hours: Informal transit runs roughly dawn to 9-10pm, with limited service after dark
transit.pay: Cash fares paid directly to the driver at fixed low rates per route
transit.map: No official transit map; routes are learned locally or from drivers
transit.note: There is no formal transit authority; the city's wide boulevards mean much travel is by private car or taxi

air: Yamoussoukro Airport (ASK), domestic flights to Abidjan
train: No passenger rail service currently operating
bus: Intercity coaches (UTB, MTT) connect to Abidjan (~2.5-3 hrs), Bouaké, and other cities

tip.r: Tipping isn't customary, but rounding up or leaving small change for good service is welcomed, especially at hotels and restaurants used by visitors.

tagline: Lithuania's ice-free Baltic port and gateway to the Curonian Spit

taxi.fareNote: Metered street taxis are available, but the Bolt app is widely used and usually cheaper and faster.

emergency.note: 112 is the unified emergency number for police, fire, and medical services across Lithuania.

hood_landmark.New Town: Meridianas sailing ship on the Danė River
hood_landmark.Fishing Village: Old fishermen's wharf along the Danė

hood_desc: The compact historic core with half-timbered German-style houses, Theatre Square, and the Danė River waterfront, walkable and full of cafés.
The main commercial district beyond the old walls, with shopping streets, the central market, and everyday city life.
A quiet seaside residential area north of downtown with a long sandy beach popular with locals for evening walks.
Reached by ferry across the harbor strait, this forested spit area holds the Sea Museum, dolphinarium, and dunes leading toward Nida.
A riverside strip near the old fishing harbor that has become the city's bar and restaurant hub, especially lively in summer.

transit.pay: Contactless bank-card tap or e-ticket app; single tickets also sold by the driver
transit.note: Small passenger ferries shuttle across the harbor strait between downtown and Smiltynė/the Curonian Spit

train: Rail connections to Vilnius (~4.5-5 hrs) and Šiauliai; limited international service
bus: Frequent intercity buses to Vilnius, Kaunas, and Riga; Ecolines/Lux Express regional coaches
ferry: DFDS ferry service to Kiel, Germany and Karlshamn, Sweden

tip.r: Tipping isn't obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% in restaurants is a welcome gesture for good service.

tagline: The Pearl of the South, a UNESCO-listed neoclassical port city on a broad bay

taxi.fareNote: Official Cubataxi cars sometimes use meters, but most rides (including classic-car almendrones) are negotiated in cash before departure, usually in USD or CUP equivalent.

emergency.note: Cuba has no single unified number: dial 106 for police and 104 for ambulance/medical emergencies.

hood_landmark.Pueblo Nuevo: Parque José Martí & Cathedral of the Purísima Concepción

hood_desc: Cienfuegos' UNESCO-listed historic core, built around the leafy Parque José Martí and its neoclassical cathedral, theater, and government buildings. Nearly every major sight, casa particular, and restaurant is within walking distance. It's the natural base for a short stay.

An elegant, tree-lined peninsula jutting into Cienfuegos Bay, lined with early 20th-century mansions including the Moorish-style Palacio de Valle. It has a slower, residential feel with sea breezes and sunset views over the water.

The city's grand central boulevard, one of the longest and widest in Cuba, connecting the historic center to Punta Gorda. Lined with shops, ice-cream stands, and colonnaded buildings, it fills with strolling locals in the evening.

A mostly residential, working-class neighborhood a short walk from the tourist core, offering an everyday look at Cuban life away from the sights. Home to local markets and modest housing rather than colonial architecture.
The bayside promenade where cienfuegueros gather at dusk to fish, chat, and watch the sunset. A cluster of seafood paladares (private restaurants) has grown up along this stretch in recent years.

transit.map: No official app; the compact historic center is best explored on foot
transit.note: Public transit is unreliable; most visitors walk, bike, or take taxis/horse carriages within the historic center.

air: Jaime González Airport (CFG) - limited international/charter flights; most visitors fly into Havana (HAV) and connect by road (~3.5 hr)
train: Slow, unreliable rail line to Havana; not recommended for tourists
bus: Viazul long-distance buses connect to Havana, Trinidad, Santa Clara and other cities

ride.avail: none (no rideshare apps operate in Cuba)

tip.r: Around 10% in restaurants is standard and appreciated; tip in cash (USD/EUR preferred over CUP) since local wages are very low. Also common to tip casa particular hosts, taxi drivers, and musicians.

tagline: UNESCO trading port where Malay, Chinese, Portuguese, and Dutch heritage collide

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis exist but many drivers prefer flat negotiated fares, especially with tourists; Grab is more reliable and transparent for pricing.

emergency.note: 999 is Malaysia's unified emergency number for police, ambulance, and fire (994 is an alternate fire-specific line).

hood_desc: Malacca's UNESCO-listed historic core, home to the red Dutch Square with Christ Church and the Stadthuys, plus the ruins of the Portuguese fort A Famosa. St. Paul's Hill offers sweeping views over the Straits of Malacca, and most museums are within walking distance.

The heart of Malacca's Peranakan (Baba-Nyonya) heritage, lined with antique shops, clan houses, and colorful shophouses. On Friday-Sunday nights it transforms into the bustling Jonker Walk Night Market with street food and live music.

A pocket of traditional Malay stilt houses just across the Malacca River from the tourist core, centered on the century-old Villa Sentosa show house. It offers a quiet, slower-paced glimpse of pre-colonial kampung life.

A laid-back beach stretch a short drive from downtown, famous for roadside stalls selling fresh coconut shake, a Malacca specialty, and casual seafood. Popular for sunset views over the Straits and a younger café-going crowd.

Home to the Portuguese Settlement (Padang St. Jose), where descendants of 16th-century Portuguese settlers maintain a distinct Kristang culture and cuisine. The waterfront square hosts nightly seafood dinners and weekend cultural performances.

transit.hours: Buses run roughly 6am-11pm; trishaws operate into the evening, especially around Jonker Walk nights
transit.pay: Cash (Touch 'n Go card accepted on some buses)
transit.map: Panorama Melaka bus routes; the historic core is compact enough to walk
transit.note: Most UNESCO-core sights are walkable; decorated bicycle trishaws are a touristy but fun way to get around at night.

air: Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KUL) - main gateway, ~2 hr drive
Malacca International Airport (MKZ) - very limited scheduled flights
train: No direct rail into the city; nearest KTM station is Tampin, about 38 km away
bus: Frequent express buses from Kuala Lumpur, Singapore, and Johor Bahru to Melaka Sentral terminal

tip.r: Tipping isn't expected; a 10% service charge plus tax is often already added to restaurant bills. Rounding up for taxis/Grab or small tips for exceptional service are appreciated but not required.

tagline: Gateway city beneath the near-perfect cone of Mayon Volcano

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis are scarce; tricycles (motorcycle sidecars) are the main short-distance transport with fixed or lightly negotiated fares, and Grab is available for point-to-point city rides.

emergency.note: 911 is the Philippines' nationwide emergency hotline covering police, fire, and medical services.

hood_desc: The modern commercial heart of Legazpi, built up after WWII around Peñaranda Park, with government offices, malls, and the city's main hotels. It's the most convenient base for exploring the rest of the city, with Mayon Volcano views on clear days.

The original town center dating to Spanish colonial times, centered on the 18th-century Sto. Domingo de Guzman Church and a scattering of ancestral houses. It has a quieter, more historic feel than the newer port area a few kilometers away.

A waterfront leisure complex built on a former pier, with a boardwalk, shops, restaurants, and a small amusement park facing Legazpi Bay with Mayon Volcano as backdrop. Popular for sunset views and weekend strolls.

A bayside barangay at the foot of Lignon Hill Nature Park, where a short hike or shuttle ride leads to sweeping panoramic views of Mayon Volcano and the city. Calmer and more residential than downtown.
A road lined with restaurants, cafes, and bars that has become Legazpi's go-to strip for evening dining and casual nightlife, popular for trying Bicol's famously spicy, coconut-milk-heavy cuisine.

transit.map: No official app; jeepney routes are known locally by destination barangay
transit.note: Tricycles are the easiest way to get around the city; jeepneys serve fixed routes cheaply; Grab is available for app-based rides.

air: Bicol International Airport (LGP) - direct flights from Manila and Cebu
train: No functioning long-distance passenger rail currently serves the Bicol region
bus: Overnight buses connect to Manila (9-12 hr) and other Bicol/Luzon cities
ferry: Limited inter-island connections via nearby Tabaco and Matnog ports (e.g., to Masbate, Samar)

tip.s: not obligatory but increasingly expected in tourism
tip.r: A 10% tip in restaurants is appreciated (some already add a service charge); rounding up for tricycles/taxis and small tips for tour guides and hotel staff are customary.

tagline: Faded colonial grandeur on a river island where Africa met Europe

taxi.fareNote: Agree the fare before departing since meters are rarely used; colorful horse-drawn calèches are a fun and common way to get around the historic island

emergency.note: Dial 17 for police and 15 for SAMU medical emergencies; medical facilities are limited, so travel insurance with evacuation coverage is strongly recommended

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed historic island packed with fading French colonial buildings, the Governor's Palace, and the Grande Mosquée; this is the heart of Saint-Louis and its main draw for visitors.
The mainland district connected to the island by the Faidherbe Bridge, home to the main market, train station, and everyday commercial life away from the tourist core.
A dense, vibrant fishing village on the narrow Langue de Barbarie sandspit, famous for its colorful wooden pirogues lining the beach at dawn and dusk.
A quieter residential and beachfront area near the river mouth, popular for its lighthouse and calmer stretch of coastline.
A rural area on the outskirts of town near the road to Gandiol, known for eco-lodges and access to nearby national parks and bird sanctuaries.

transit.pay: Cash only; fares negotiated or fixed by route
transit.map: No official transit map; ask locals or hotel staff
transit.note: Public transit is informal; most visitors walk the compact island or use taxis and calèches for longer trips

air: Blaise Diagne International Airport (DSS) in Dakar, ~4 hours away
bus: Frequent buses and shared sept-place taxis from Dakar (~4 hours)

tip.r: Round up or leave 5-10% at restaurants catering to tourists; not expected at small local eateries

tagline: City of dreaming spires, centuries of scholarship, and cobbled college quads

taxi.fareNote: Licensed black cabs can be hailed on the street or found at ranks; minicabs are cheaper but must be pre-booked by phone or app

emergency.note: Dial 999 for emergencies (police, ambulance, fire); call 111 for non-urgent medical advice via the NHS

hood_desc: Home to the historic university colleges, the Bodleian Library, and Radcliffe Camera. Pedestrianized streets and the Covered Market make it easy to explore on foot, though it gets crowded with tourists and students alike.
A charming Victorian-era neighborhood of terraced houses along the Oxford Canal, known for indie cafes, the Phoenix Picturehouse cinema, and a bohemian, arty feel.
A diverse, lively area southeast of the centre with some of Oxford's best curry houses, live music venues, and student-friendly bars along Cowley Road.
An affluent residential suburb north of the centre with boutique shops, delis, and a village-like high street popular with families.
A hillside suburb east of the centre, home to the John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford Brookes University, and the famous fibreglass Headington Shark sculpture.

transit.hours: Roughly 5:30am-midnight, reduced service late night and Sundays
transit.pay: Contactless card, mobile app, or cash on board
transit.note: Oxford has no metro or tram; buses, walking, and cycling are the main ways to get around, along with Park & Ride from the edge of the city

train: Direct trains to London Paddington (~1 hour)
Direct trains to Birmingham, Reading, and Manchester
bus: Oxford Tube and National Express 24-hour coach services to London

tip.r: Restaurants often add a 10-12.5% service charge; if not included, 10% is appreciated. Not customary for taxis or pubs beyond rounding up

tagline: Ancient shogunate capital of temples, the Great Buddha, and seaside calm

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are reliable, spotlessly clean, and metered with no need to tip; rear doors open automatically

emergency.note: Dial 110 for police, 119 for ambulance/fire; English support is available via the Japan Visitor Hotline 050-3816-2787

hood_desc: The bustling heart of the city and main arrival point by train, with the pedestrian shopping street Komachi-dori packed with souvenir shops and street food leading toward Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine.

Home to Kamakura's most famous sight, the towering bronze Great Buddha at Kotoku-in, as well as Hase-dera Temple with its hillside gardens and ocean views, a short ride from the station on the Enoden line.
A tranquil, forested area north of the station dotted with major Zen temples like Engaku-ji and Kencho-ji, popular for quiet contemplative walks especially during autumn foliage.
A laid-back residential beach neighborhood east of Yuigahama, quieter than its neighbor, with a family-friendly stretch of sand and views toward the Miura Peninsula.
Kamakura's main beach district, lined with surf shops and casual cafes, drawing a younger, laid-back crowd especially in the warmer months.

transit.pay: IC cards (Suica/Pasmo) tap-in tap-out, or single tickets
transit.note: The scenic Enoden tram connects Kamakura Station to Hase, Yuigahama, and Enoshima; JR trains link Kamakura directly to Tokyo and Yokohama

train: JR Yokosuka Line direct to Tokyo (~1 hour) and Yokohama (~25 min)
bus: Airport limousine buses run from Haneda/Narita to nearby Yokohama, then onward by train

tip.s: not customary, can be considered rude
tip.r: Tipping is not expected anywhere in Japan, including restaurants, taxis, and hotels; excellent service is standard and included
